name: Festival Stone of Evensong
title: Festival Stone of Evensong
summary: The Festival Stone of Evensong 'guards the shore of the river we call Prosper ... near the end of the ruins of a temple complex built over the river; a monolithic head statue suggests that this was not a temple in the favor of the High Empyrean' (Alatar Locke). In the kit the stone and its Anniversary glow stand on the mud shore at z 27.9; south of it a 100 m line of ruins stands in the running water: a moss-brick block, ancient seals and stubs, bamboo islands and, at the south end, a gateway of four 10 m stone wall blocks with a 7 m monolithic head rock between them.

shots.standingOrder: Fly north 20 m above the River Prosper straight over the drowned temple gateway, its twin stone walls and monolithic head, toward the Evensong Festival Stone on the shore; stay 10 m above the walls.
shots.notes: Flagship water shot of the batch: level pass due north 20 m above the River Prosper (running water, z 28) straight over the drowned temple gateway - twin 10 m stone wall blocks, the 7 m monolithic head rock between them, bamboo islands - with the gimbal tracking the gateway down through vertical (yaw-slew <= 40 deg/s) and the Evensong Festival Stone and its glow on the shore ahead. Low morning sun from the east side-lights the walls and glints on the water. shots.standingOrder: From the east bank pan right off the bamboo and broken temple stones in the river onto the glowing Evensong Festival Stone at the water's edge; the camera holds still and only turns.
shots.notes: Pan from the east bank (35 m ESE of the stone, 5.6 m above the mud shore): the head starts 40 deg left on the bamboo islands and broken temple stones standing in the river and swings right onto the Festival Stone and its Anniversary glow at the water's edge, the morning sun behind the lens. The camera never moves. The far south gateway is outside the frame; the middle ruins carry the first half.
